text:
emily.engineer: Hey folks - had a weird hotel situation on my trip. Hotel placed a $200 pre-auth for incidentals on my personal card because the company card was declined at check-in. Final bill ended up $72 (room + tax). The hotel released the remaining hold but my bank shows the $200 pending authorization for 7 days then it disappeared (no final charge). How do I file this? Do I need to attach the bank "pending" screenshot? Also, will finance reimburse the $72 to my personal card or should I put it on the company card retroactively?

lydia.peopleops: Sorry that happened. Short version: we reimburse valid charges whether on personal or company card. For pre-auths that never converted into a charge, you don't get reimbursed for the hold (because no actual charge). For your expense, attach the hotel folio/final invoice and a screenshot of your personal card showing the final $72 charge. If your bank later converts the pending auth into a charge, update the report.

lydia.peopleops: Requirements we need: 1) final itemized hotel folio (with folio number/date) 2) proof of payment that shows the actual settled charge (bank/cc statement screenshot or company card charge). If the settled amount matches the folio, finance will process reimbursement to the payment method on the expense report (select "personal card").

emily.engineer: Got it. The weird part is the pending auth disappeared (no settled charge). I only have the folio and the hotel's statement that the pre-auth was authorization-only. My bank statement doesn't show a $72 charge because they never charged it (I paid in cash at checkout), but the hotel folio has a folio number and shows room + tax = $72. Is that enough?

receipts-bot: receipt uploaded: 2161234600_hilton-chi-folio.pdf

tom.finance: Thanks for the upload. If the hotel issued a final folio and you have a receipt/scanned folio, that's acceptable. If payment was in cash, we need an attestation in the expense report explaining payment method OR a merchant receipt that indicates cash collected. If you don't have a cash receipt, include the hotel folio plus this short attestation: "I paid the final hotel balance of $72 in cash on 2025-10-02; pre-authorization of $200 on my personal card was authorization-only and was released by the hotel." Finance will triage.

raj.manager: I can confirm Emily was on company travel and this is work-related. I approve the reimbursement.

lydia.peopleops: Note on timelines: banks hold auths for different windows (usually 5-10 days). A disappeared pending auth without a settled charge means no reimbursement is due for that auth. If you did pay the balance in cash and want reimbursement to a bank account, choose "reimburse to bank" in Expensify (or our tool) and attach bank details.

tom.finance: Also: if you want reimbursement to your personal card (refund onto card), finance policy prefers ACH to your bank account instead of refund to personal card. Please select direct deposit and add your ACH details in the report. If you accidentally charged the company card later, we'll offset it.

emily.engineer: Thanks. Last question: should I also include a screenshot of the bank page that showed the original pending $200 auth (even though it's gone now)? Thought that might prove the hotel did pre-auth.

lydia.peopleops: Yes, include any screenshots you have. It helps with vendor reconciliations. Put everything in one expense report entry and mark it "hotel - preauth released, final folio attached". We'll process once manager approval (raj) is present and docs are complete.

emily.engineer: Perfect. Uploading bank screenshot + folio now. Thanks everyone!
